sources.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization

extracted: Section 1 (boxed functional forms R_bon(d)=d(alpha_bon - beta_bon d), R_RL(d)=d(alpha_RL - beta_RL log d), d=sqrt(KL)); Section 2 (gold RM = 6B, proxy RMs 3M-3B, policy 1.2B, 90,000 comparisons); Section 3.2 (policy 1.2B and data 90,000 held constant; alpha_RL held constant across RM sizes); Figure 1 panels (a) BoN and (b) RL (files a_bon_rmsweep.png, a_rl_rmsweep.png, 2700x1800 px); Figure 3 panels (a) alpha_bon, (b) beta_bon, (c) beta_RL versus RM size (files a_bon_rmsweep_fit_alpha.png, a_bon_rmsweep_fit_beta.png, a_rl_rmsweep_fit_beta.png, 450x300 px); Appendix, Figure 12 caption (BoN max gold score = alpha_bon/(2 beta_bon)); Section 3.1 (BoN validated to n=60,000, KL about 10 nats).
tool: /Users/jadtarifi/Documents/Claude/intrinsic-alignment/scripts/digitize_gao2022_fig1.py (PIL+numpy+scipy): plot area located by seaborn background colour, tick positions from white grid lines, sqrt-scaled x axis mapped as pixel = a + b*sqrt(KL); each RM size isolated by its legend RGB (saturated colour for gold curves, alpha~0.128 faded colour for proxy dashed curves), column-wise median row -> (KL, score); Figure 3 coefficient dots isolated by a filled-disk test that suppresses the thin regression line, centroid -> value.
notes: The paper publishes the functional forms but no numeric coefficient table; alpha_bon, beta_bon and beta_RL per RM size were digitized from the dots in Figure 3 (a)-(c) (450x300 px source, roughly 0.0004-0.001 per pixel), and the Figure 3 log-linear regression lines have no published coefficients so no alpha(N)/beta(N) relation is recorded. alpha_RL is not plotted anywhere; the paper only says it is held constant across RM sizes. The value 0.385 here is derived: a least-squares fit of R=d(alpha - beta ln d) to the digitized gold RL curves of all nine RM sizes with beta fixed to the Figure 3(c) values; per-size fixed-beta fits gave alpha between 0.379 and 0.395. Treat the RL gold fit curves as a reconstruction of the published fit, accurate to roughly 0.05 in RM score at KL>60. Sanity checks: BoN peak gold score alpha^2/(4 beta) for the 3M RM = 0.50 at d=2.05 (KL 4.2), matching the plotted 3M curve; BoN fits from Figure 3 reproduce the digitized gold curves with RMSE 0.005-0.025; free fits of the digitized BoN curves agree with the Figure 3 dots within about 0.015 (alpha) and 0.008 (beta). x is d = sqrt(KL) in nats^0.5 (the paper draws KL on a square-root axis, so d is linear in the figure). Domain of the paper plots: RL KL 0-100 (d 0-10; individual runs end between KL 78 and 99); BoN KL 0-10 (d 0-3.16, n up to 60,000). Gold "digitized curve" series are the paper's thick gold data lines (the thin published fit line has the same colour and is nearly coincident, so both are merged in the column median); they are provided as a check on the fit series. Proxy series are digitized from the faded dashed proxy lines. Their y-values lie on real proxy curves, but attribution to a specific RM size relies on faded colours that differ by only a few RGB units between neighbouring sizes, so adjacent sizes may be swapped and coverage is sparse where the dashed lines overlap the gold lines (low KL); lower confidence than the gold series. The paper found no satisfactory functional form for proxy scores, so none is given. The proxy RMs are labelled by the legend (3M ... 3B); the Figure 3 x-positions imply the largest RM is nearer 2.5B than 3B. Gold RM = 6B RM from Ouyang et al. (2022); RM scores recentred so the initial policy scores 0 and gold score variance unit-normalised; KL penalty 0 for RL. Colour roles are semantic: proxy = optimised proxy RM score, truth = gold RM score.

y.label: RM score (gold RM units, initial policy = 0)
